title: Sole Parent Support entitlement (Social Security Act 2018 ss 29-32), OpenFisca Aotearoa; second coder

attributes.name: age
attributes.source: sole_parent_support.py:37 and :118-130 (s29(d)): age at period.first_day >= entitlements.social_security.sole_parent_support.age_threshold = 20 (parameters/entitlements/social_security/sole_parent_support/age_threshold.yaml, from 2018)

attributes.name: principal_caregiver
attributes.source: sole_parent_support.py:183 (s30), read at period.first_month of each day; variable social_security__principal_caregiver, interpretation/relationship.py:28 (Schedule 2)

attributes.name: child_age
attributes.source: sole_parent_support.py:178-181 (s30): child's age at the day < social_security.sole_parent_support.child_age_threshold = 14 (parameters/social_security/sole_parent_support/child_age_threshold.yml, from 2018-11-26)

output.name: sole_parent_support__entitled
output.source: sole_parent_support.py:23-39, formula_2018_11_26 = requirement AND split_care AND residential_requirement AND age_threshold, for the principal P

period.why: the only period used by the official tests; formula_2018_11_26 applies

household.value: family F with principal P and one member C in the child role; P is the subject; every other input at its declared default
household.why: s30 and s32 read the family; with one child, social_security__dependent_children of P is 0 or 1, so split care (s32) reduces to P holding the principal role, and the other parent of s32 does not arise

principal_caregiver period.why: the dependent child requirement reads it at the first month of each day of 2019-W05, which spans January and February 2019; the official tests set it the same way

notes: Second-coder conversion (blinded). Choices and sources in CONVERSION_2.md.
